key_insight: A room-aware Transformer achieved the highest or tied activity-recognition accuracy in 9 of 15 home-window comparisons, but no model was uniformly best.
clinical_relevance: Ambient-sensor activity recognition may support longitudinal assessment of everyday functioning in adults with mild neurocognitive disorder, though clinical utility remains unestablished.
method: Aligned motion, environmental, and door-contact sensor data with activity logs harmonized into eight categories.
Compared room-aware and global Transformers with a stacked LSTM, training models separately for each home.
Evaluated 10-, 30-, and 60-minute windows using day-separated training, validation, and chronological test sets.
evidence_signal: Across five homes, 92,765 minute-level observations and 67 annotated home-days, room-aware test accuracy ranged from 0.27 to 0.57, with micro-AUC of 0.57–0.82 and macro-AUC of 0.54–0.78.
watch_item: The small, home-specific evaluation leaves generalization to new residents, layouts, and sensor configurations uncertain.
paper_title: Room-Aware Transformer for Activities of Daily Living Recognition in Adults with Mild Neurocognitive Disorder Using Ambient Sensors: Development and Evaluation Study
